items.definition: A question built on what the other person just said, which shows you were listening.
items.example: You said you moved last year — what was it like at first?

items.definition: A short sound or remark that shows you are following without taking the turn, such as 'mm' or 'really'.
items.example: You say 'really?' and then let them keep going.

items.definition: A prepared sentence that ends a conversation politely while leaving the door open for another meeting.
items.example: It was really nice meeting you — see you around.

items.definition: A comfortable relationship between people, built when each can predict how the other will behave.
items.example: We had no topic in common, but we talked for twenty minutes and had instant rapport.
